questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India directs the State to provide public assistance to its citizens in case of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement, within the limits of its economic capacity and development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 41**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 41** is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in the Indian Constitution.
 
• It directs the State to provide **public assistance** in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement.
 
• The provision is subject to the **State's economic capacity and development**.
 
• It emphasizes the State's responsibility to ensure social security and welfare for its citizens.
 
• Article 41 reflects the vision of a welfare state as enshrined in the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• DPSPs are non-justiciable provisions in Part IV of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They aim to establish a socio-economic democracy and act as guidelines for the State in governance.
 
• Examples include provisions for education, health, social security, and protection of the environment.
 
 
 
• **Economic Capacity:**
 
 
• Refers to the financial ability of the State to implement welfare measures.
 
• It ensures that the directives are realistic and aligned with available resources.
 
 
 
• **Welfare State:**
 
 
• The concept of a welfare state is enshrined in the Preamble and DPSPs of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The goal is to promote social and economic justice for all citizens.
 
 
 
• **Related Articles:**
 
 
• **Article 39:** Promotes equal pay for equal work and adequate livelihood.
 
• **Article 43:** Directs the State to ensure a living wage and a decent standard of life for workers.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about the Ozone layer are true?

Statement A: It is found in the stratosphere.

Statement B: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are responsible for ozone hole.

Statement C: Ozone layer is found around 15-30 km above the earth's surface.

Statement D: Ozone layer is expected not to recover anymore now.

options.text: Only statements A, B and C
Only statement B, C and D

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only statements A, B, and C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement A:** The ozone layer is primarily found in the **stratosphere**, which lies approximately 10-50 km above the Earth's surface, with the ozone concentration peaking at 15-30 km.
 
• **Statement B:** Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are a significant cause of ozone depletion, leading to the formation of the **ozone hole**, especially over Antarctica.
 
• **Statement C:** The ozone layer is located in the stratosphere at altitudes of about **15-30 km** above Earth, where it absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the Sun.
 
• **Statement D is incorrect:** Studies and international agreements like the Montreal Protocol have led to a reduction in ozone-depleting substances, and the ozone layer is expected to recover gradually by mid-21st century.
 
• The correct answer includes statements **A, B, and C**, as they are scientifically accurate and backed by research.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ozone Layer:** A protective layer of ozone (O₃) molecules in the stratosphere that absorbs and blocks the majority of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV-B and UV-C) radiation.
 
• **Ozone Hole:** A region of significant ozone depletion, primarily over Antarctica, caused by chemical reactions involving CFCs and other ozone-depleting substances (ODS).
 
• **Montreal Protocol (1987):** An international treaty designed to phase out the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances. It is considered one of the most successful environmental agreements to date.
 
• **UV Radiation:** Excessive UV exposure can lead to health issues such as skin cancer, cataracts, and immune system suppression, as well as environmental effects like reduced crop yields.
 
• **Ozone Layer Recovery:** Due to global efforts under the Montreal Protocol, the ozone layer is showing signs of recovery and is projected to return to 1980 levels by 2050 for most regions.

questions.question: Which book has been authored by Shovana Narayan and Geetika Kalha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Mythology through Classical Dance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Indian Mythology through Classical Dance** is co-authored by Shovana Narayan, a renowned Kathak dancer, and Geetika Kalha, an accomplished bureaucrat and scholar.
 
• The book explores the deep connection between Indian classical dance forms and their roots in Indian mythology and cultural heritage.
 
• It highlights how ancient Indian epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata, as well as Puranic stories, have been depicted through classical dance gestures, expressions, and performances.
 
• Shovana Narayan is a Padma Shri awardee, celebrated for her contribution to Kathak, while Geetika Kalha has an extensive academic background in Indian culture.
 
• The book is a significant contribution to understanding the interplay of dance, mythology, and tradition in Indian art forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shovana Narayan:**

 
 
• She is one of India's leading exponents of Kathak and has been honored with the Padma Shri for her contributions to the field of classical dance.
 
• Her works often combine rigorous research with artistic expression, making her an authority on dance and its historical significance.
 
 
 
• **Geetika Kalha:**
 
 
• A retired IAS officer with expertise in Indian culture and heritage.
 
• She has collaborated on various projects to document and preserve India's rich artistic traditions.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Dance:**
 
 
• The eight recognized classical dance forms of India include Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, Kathakali, Manipuri, Kuchipudi, Mohiniyattam, and Sattriya.
 
• These dances are deeply rooted in the Natya Shastra, an ancient Sanskrit text on performing arts, attributed to Sage Bharata.
 
 
 
• **Mythology in Dance:**
 
 
• Indian classical dances often draw themes and narratives from epics like the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas.
 
• Gestures (Mudras), facial expressions, and rhythmic movements are used to convey stories and emotions inspired by mythology.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• Books like "Indian Mythology through Classical Dance" serve to preserve and promote the understanding of India's cultural heritage.
 
• They provide insights into how traditional art forms contribute to the continuity of India's spiritual and artistic legacy.

questions.question: In which of the following sessions of Congress did the Party issue a call to celebrate 26th January as 'Purna Swaraj Day'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lahore 1929**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The resolution to celebrate 26th January as 'Purna Swaraj Day' (Complete Independence Day) was passed during the **Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress in December 1929**.
 
• The session was presided over by **Jawaharlal Nehru**, who played a key role in the declaration of Purna Swaraj.
 
• The Congress declared **complete independence (Purna Swaraj) as its ultimate goal**, rejecting the dominion status proposed by the British government.
 
• It was decided that 26th January 1930 would be observed as **Independence Day**, and the day was marked by public meetings and the reading of the Purna Swaraj pledge.
 
• This event laid the foundation for India’s quest for independence, and later, the Constitution of India came into effect on 26th January 1950, marking it as Republic Day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Purna Swaraj Declaration:**

 
 
• The resolution for complete independence was a reaction to the British government's failure to meet the demands of the Nehru Report (1928).
 
• The declaration affirmed India's determination to fight for complete freedom from colonial rule.
 
• The Purna Swaraj pledge emphasized civil disobedience as a means to achieve independence.
 
 
 
• **Lahore Session of 1929:**
 
 
• This session of the Congress was significant as it marked a shift from dominion status to complete independence as the goal of the freedom struggle.
 
• It was held on the banks of the Ravi River in Lahore (now in Pakistan).
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was elected the president of the session, underscoring his rising prominence in the freedom movement.
 
 
 
• **26th January in Indian History:**
 
 
• The date was chosen to signify the importance of the Purna Swaraj resolution.
 
• Post-independence, the date was adopted as the day when the Indian Constitution came into effect in 1950, making India a sovereign, democratic republic.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Purna Swaraj Resolution:**
 
 
• The resolution galvanized the Indian population, especially the youth, towards the struggle for complete independence.
 
• It marked the beginning of mass participation in anti-colonial movements like the Civil Disobedience Movement (1930).

questions.question: Padma Subrahmanyam is associated with which dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Padma Subrahmanyam is a renowned Indian classical dancer and is widely known for her expertise in **Bharatanatyam**.
 
• She is credited with reviving Bharatanatyam by integrating traditional texts, sculptures, and dance forms into the modern-day style.
 
• Padma Subrahmanyam has been honored with numerous awards, including the Padma Shri (1981) and Padma Bhushan (2003), for her contribution to Indian classical dance.
 
• Her unique style, "Bharata Nrityam," is inspired by the Natya Shastra, an ancient treatise on performing arts.
 
• She is also a scholar, musician, and choreographer, contributing significantly to the preservation and promotion of Bharatanatyam globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**

 
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating from Tamil Nadu.
 
• The term "Bharatanatyam" is derived from "Bha" (Bhava - expression), "Ra" (Raga - melody), "Ta" (Tala - rhythm), and "Natyam" (dance).
 
• It was traditionally performed in temples as an offering to deities and as a form of storytelling through intricate hand gestures (mudras) and facial expressions.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in the Natya Shastra, an ancient Sanskrit text on performing arts by Bharata Muni.
 
 
 
• **Natya Shastra**
 
 
• Natya Shastra is an ancient Indian treatise on performing arts, written by sage Bharata.
 
• It details various aspects of dance, drama, and music, including techniques, expressions, and aesthetics.
 
• The principles of Bharatanatyam are heavily influenced by the Natya Shastra, emphasizing the integration of body movements, rhythm, and expressions.
 
 
 
• **Padma Subrahmanyam's Contributions**
 
 
• She is recognized for her research on the 108 karanas (basic dance movements) mentioned in the Natya Shastra.
 
• Her work has bridged the gap between ancient dance traditions and modern Bharatanatyam practices.
 
• She has authored several books and articles, contributing to the academic understanding of Indian classical dance.
 
 
 
• **Global Impact**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is now performed globally and is recognized as a symbol of India's cultural heritage.
 
• Artists like Padma Subrahmanyam have played a crucial role in making this dance form accessible and admired worldwide.

questions.question: In 2023, Government of India has announced to set up a/an __________ DigiLocker for use by MSMEs, large businesses, and charitable trusts to store and share documents online securely.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Entity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 2023, the Government of India announced the launch of an **Entity DigiLocker** for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), large businesses, and charitable trusts.
 
• The **Entity DigiLocker** aims to help organizations securely store and share official documents online.
 
• It is an extension of the existing DigiLocker platform, which was primarily designed for individual use.
 
• This initiative is part of India's broader push towards **digital governance** and ease of doing business.
 
• The platform ensures **data security** and compliance, providing users with a safe and reliable environment for document management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DigiLocker:**

 
 
• DigiLocker is a flagship initiative under the Digital India program by the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY).
 
• It allows Indian citizens to securely store and share digital documents, such as Aadhaar, PAN card, and educational certificates.
 
• Users can access their documents anytime, anywhere through the DigiLocker mobile app or website.
 
• The platform also supports government-to-citizen document issuance and verification.
 
 
 
• **Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs):**
 
 
• MSMEs are classified based on investment in plant/machinery or equipment and annual turnover.
 
• They contribute significantly to India’s GDP, exports, and employment generation.
 
• The government provides various schemes to support MSMEs, such as credit assistance, skill development, and technology upgradation.
 
 
 
• **Digital Governance in India:**
 
 
• Digital governance refers to the use of digital technologies to enhance the delivery of government services to citizens and businesses.
 
• Programs like Digital India aim to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
 
• Key initiatives include Aadhaar, e-Governance projects, and the Unified Payments Interface (UPI).
 
 
 
• **Charitable Trusts:**
 
 
• Charitable trusts in India operate for philanthropic purposes, such as education, healthcare, and poverty alleviation.
 
• They are registered under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, and are eligible for tax benefits under the Income Tax Act.
 
• The Entity DigiLocker offers a streamlined way for trusts to manage and share compliance-related documents.

questions.question: Oak and chestnut trees are found in which type of forest in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Montane forests**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Montane forests** are typically found in mountainous regions of India, specifically at elevations ranging from 1500 to 3500 meters.
 
• Oak and chestnut trees are prominent species in **temperate montane forests**, which are characterized by cool and moist climatic conditions.
 
• These forests are generally located in parts of the Himalayan ranges, where the climate supports the growth of oak and chestnut trees.
 
• Montane forests are divided into **two categories**: temperate forests at higher altitudes and tropical montane forests at lower altitudes.
 
• Other prominent trees found in montane forests include rhododendrons, deodar, spruce, and fir.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Montane Forests Overview:**

 
 
• Montane forests are ecosystems found in mountainous regions where altitude plays a critical role in vegetation distribution.
 
• These forests are known for their diverse flora and fauna, which are adapted to cooler temperatures and high humidity.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan Montane Ecosystem:**
 
 
• The Himalayan montane forests host a variety of plant species like oak, chestnut, pine, and cedar.
 
• They act as a vital water source for rivers and contribute significantly to India's biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Types of Montane Forests in India:**
 
 
• **Temperate Montane Forests:** Found at higher altitudes, featuring oak, chestnut, and coniferous trees.
 
• **Tropical Montane Forests:** Located at lower altitudes with species like bamboo and tropical hardwoods.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance:**
 
 
• Montane forests prevent soil erosion and regulate the local climate by retaining moisture.
 
• They serve as habitats for endangered species, such as snow leopards and red pandas.

questions.question: Which of the following types of volcanic eruptions of Earth's volcanoes are most explosive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Caldera**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **Caldera** is a large volcanic depression formed when a volcano's magma chamber empties and the ground above collapses.
 
• Caldera eruptions are the **most explosive** and catastrophic volcanic events, capable of ejecting enormous amounts of ash, lava, and gases.
 
• Famous examples of caldera eruptions include the **Yellowstone Caldera** in the USA and the **Tambora eruption** of 1815 in Indonesia.
 
• These eruptions can significantly impact global climate by injecting vast quantities of ash and sulfur dioxide into the atmosphere, leading to phenomena like "volcanic winters."
 
• Caldera-forming events are rare but are associated with the most severe volcanic hazards, including pyroclastic flows and widespread ashfall.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Volcanic Terminologies:**

 
 
• A **Dyke** is a vertical or steeply inclined intrusion of magma that cuts through pre-existing rock layers.
 
• A **Lopolith** is a large, saucer-shaped intrusion of igneous rock, typically associated with less explosive volcanic activity.
 
• **Flood basalt provinces** refer to extensive regions covered by layers of basaltic lava, formed by effusive eruptions rather than explosive ones.
 
 
 
• **Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI):**
 
 
• The VEI is a scale used to measure the explosiveness of volcanic eruptions, ranging from 0 (non-explosive) to 8 (cataclysmic).
 
• Caldera-forming eruptions typically score a VEI of 6 or higher.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Caldera Eruptions:**
 
 
• They can create massive craters, sometimes filled with water to form caldera lakes (e.g., Crater Lake in Oregon, USA).
 
• Long-term impacts include changes in atmospheric composition and significant cooling of the Earth's climate.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Major Calderas:**
 
 
• The **Yellowstone Caldera** is a supervolcano located in Wyoming, USA, with the potential for future catastrophic eruptions.
 
• The **Toba Caldera** in Indonesia erupted approximately 74,000 years ago, causing a volcanic winter and a significant drop in global temperatures.

questions.question: What is the term 'ace' commonly associated within sports?

options.text: A high jump technique in athletics

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A fast serve in tennis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An 'ace' in tennis refers to a serve where the ball is served so well that the opponent cannot touch it, resulting in a direct point for the server.
 
• For a serve to be considered an ace, it must land in the service box without any fault or double fault.
 
• Aces are a key indicator of a player’s serving ability and are often recorded as a performance statistic in matches.
 
• Some of the top tennis players, such as Roger Federer, Serena Williams, and Ivo Karlović, are known for their ability to hit a high number of aces during matches.
 
• Ace serves are particularly effective on faster court surfaces like grass or hard courts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Tennis Terminologies:**

 
 
• **Double Fault:** When a player fails to deliver a valid serve twice consecutively, resulting in a point for the opponent.
 
• **Deuce:** A score of 40-40 in a game, requiring a player to win by two consecutive points to claim the game.
 
• **Break Point:** A situation where the receiving player is one point away from winning the game on the opponent's serve.
 
• **Love:** A tennis term that means zero points in a game.
 
 
 
• **Serving Techniques:**
 
 
• **Flat Serve:** A serve hit with minimal spin for maximum speed.
 
• **Slice Serve:** A serve with sidespin, causing the ball to curve in the air.
 
• **Kick Serve:** A serve with topspin, causing the ball to bounce high after hitting the court.
 
 
 
• **Fastest Recorded Aces:**
 
 
• The fastest recorded serve in tennis is 263 km/h (163.7 mph) by Sam Groth of Australia during the 2012 Busan Open Challenger.
 
• In women’s tennis, the fastest recorded serve is 210.8 km/h (131 mph) by Sabine Lisicki of Germany at the 2014 Stanford Classic.
 
 
 
• **Top Players Known for Aces:**
 
 
• **Ivo Karlović:** Holds the record for the most career aces in professional tennis.
 
• **Serena Williams:** Renowned for her powerful serves and high ace counts in women's tennis.

questions.question: Lokrang, a five-day festival organised by the Madhya Pradesh Adivasi Lok Kala Academy, begins on ______________ every year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**26th January**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lokrang** is a five-day cultural festival organized annually by the Madhya Pradesh Adivasi Lok Kala Academy.
 
• The festival begins every year on **26th January**, coinciding with India's Republic Day celebrations.
 
• **Lokrang** aims to showcase and celebrate the rich tribal and folk culture of Madhya Pradesh and other regions of India.
 
• The festival includes performances of folk music, dance, art exhibitions, and workshops featuring various tribal communities.
 
• **International artists** and participants also join the festival, adding a global touch to the cultural exchange.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Madhya Pradesh Adivasi Lok Kala Academy**

 
 
• The academy is dedicated to preserving and promoting the tribal and folk art forms of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It organizes events like Lokrang and other exhibitions to encourage cultural exchange and awareness.
 
 
 
• **Folk and Tribal Arts**
 
 
• India is home to diverse folk and tribal art forms, including music, dance, and painting.
 
• These art forms are often deeply rooted in local traditions, rituals, and community practices.
 
 
 
• **Significance of 26th January**
 
 
• 26th January marks Republic Day in India, commemorating the adoption of the Constitution in 1950.
 
• It is celebrated nationwide with parades, cultural programs, and patriotic events.
 
 
 
• **Global Cultural Exchange**
 
 
• Events like Lokrang provide a platform for international artists to interact with Indian tribal and folk communities.
 
• Such exchanges help in fostering cross-cultural understanding and appreciation.

questions.question: The Kakrapar Atomic Power Plant is located in which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kakrapar Atomic Power Plant (KAPP) is located in **Kakrapar, Surat district, Gujarat, India**.
 
• It is operated by the **Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL)**, a public sector enterprise under the Department of Atomic Energy.
 
• KAPP houses pressurized heavy water reactors (PHWRs), which use natural uranium as fuel and heavy water as both moderator and coolant.
 
• The plant's first two units, KAPS-1 and KAPS-2, began operations in **1993 and 1995, respectively**.
 
• In 2021, Unit-3 of the plant, a 700 MW PHWR, became operational, marking a significant milestone in India's nuclear energy development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pressurized Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR):**

 
 
• PHWRs are nuclear reactors that use **heavy water (deuterium oxide) as both a coolant and a neutron moderator**.
 
• They are capable of using natural uranium as fuel, making them cost-effective for countries with limited uranium enrichment infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL):**
 
 
• NPCIL is a public sector enterprise responsible for the design, construction, operation, and maintenance of nuclear power plants in India.
 
• It plays a crucial role in achieving India’s goal of increasing the share of nuclear energy in the country’s energy mix.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Energy in India:**
 
 
• India aims to significantly increase its nuclear power capacity as part of its strategy to reduce dependence on fossil fuels.
 
• The country currently has 22 operational nuclear reactors, with more under construction or planned.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• India is a member of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and follows strict safety and regulatory protocols for its nuclear plants.
 
• The development of indigenous nuclear technology, such as the PHWR, underlines India's commitment to self-reliance in the energy sector.

questions.question: The rock-cut caves in Karnataka, mainly at Badami and Aihole, were built under the patronage of the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chalukyas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The rock-cut caves at Badami and Aihole in Karnataka were constructed under the patronage of the **Chalukya dynasty**.
 
• The Early Chalukyas ruled from **6th to 8th century CE**, and their capital was originally at Aihole and later shifted to Badami.
 
• The Badami caves are a series of **four rock-cut cave temples**, showcasing Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist influences.
 
• The Chalukyas were pioneers in the **Vesara style of architecture**, which is a blend of Dravidian and Nagara architectural styles.
 
• The Badami Chalukyas also laid the foundation for temple architecture in South India that would influence later dynasties like the Rashtrakutas and Hoysalas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Badami Caves:**

 
 
• There are four caves in Badami, with three dedicated to Hindu deities (Shiva and Vishnu) and one to Jainism.
 
• The famous Nataraja sculpture with 18 arms is a highlight of Cave 1.
 
• Caves 2 and 3 are dedicated to Vishnu, with detailed carvings of his various avatars, including Trivikrama and Narasimha.
 
• Cave 4 is a Jain temple, housing a sculpture of Mahavira in a meditative posture.
 
 
 
• **Aihole:**
 
 
• Aihole is often referred to as the "Cradle of Indian Temple Architecture."
 
• It contains over 100 temples, including the famous Durga Temple and Lad Khan Temple.
 
• The Durga Temple is known for its apsidal (semi-circular) design and intricate sculptures.
 
 
 
• **Vesara Architecture:**
 
 
• It is a hybrid architectural style that combines elements of the northern Nagara and southern Dravidian styles.
 
• The Chalukyas were instrumental in developing this style, which became prominent in South India.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of the Chalukyas:**
 
 
• The Chalukyas made significant contributions to art, architecture, and culture in South India.
 
• They influenced subsequent dynasties, including the Rashtrakutas and Hoysalas, in temple construction and artistic traditions.

questions.question: Vani Jairam, who won Padma Bhushan 2023, belongs to which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vani Jairam, a legendary playback singer, was born in **Vellore, Tamil Nadu**, in 1945.
 
• She is renowned for her contribution to Indian music, having sung in over **18 Indian languages**, including Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, and Kannada.
 
• She received the **Padma Bhushan award in 2023**, the third-highest civilian honor in India, for her immense contribution to the field of music.
 
• Vani Jairam has won **three National Film Awards** and several state awards for her playback singing across various languages.
 
• Her melodious voice and versatility have made her an iconic figure in Indian cinema and music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Bhushan Award**

 
 
• The Padma Bhushan is the third-highest civilian award in India, instituted in 1954.
 
• It is conferred for distinguished service of a high order in any field including art, literature, science, and public affairs.
 
• Recipients are announced every year on the eve of Republic Day.
 
 
 
• **National Film Awards**
 
 
• India's most prestigious film awards, instituted in 1954, to honor the best in Indian cinema.
 
• Vani Jairam won the National Film Award for Best Female Playback Singer thrice for her contributions.
 
 
 
• **Contributions to Indian Music**
 
 
• Vani Jairam has collaborated with legendary composers like MS Viswanathan, RD Burman, and Ilaiyaraaja.
 
• Her notable songs include hits like "Bol Re Papihara" (Hindi), "Malligai En Mannan Mayangum" (Tamil), and "Ennenno Janmala Bandham" (Telugu).
 
 
 
• **Playback Singing**
 
 
• Playback singing is a technique in Indian cinema where singers record songs for actors to lip-sync on screen.
 
• Vani Jairam is celebrated as one of the most versatile playback singers in Indian cinema history.

questions.question: A four-carbon chain with a triple bond is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**butyne**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A four-carbon chain with a triple bond belongs to the category of **alkynes**, which are hydrocarbons containing at least one triple bond between carbon atoms.
 
• The name "butyne" is derived from the prefix "but-" indicating a four-carbon chain and the suffix "-yne" signifying the presence of a triple bond.
 
• Butyne exists in two isomeric forms: **1-butyne** (triple bond at the first carbon) and **2-butyne** (triple bond at the second carbon).
 
• Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons and are known for their reactivity due to the presence of the triple bond, which consists of one sigma bond and two pi bonds.
 
• In the IUPAC nomenclature system, the position of the triple bond is indicated using numbers, e.g., 1-butyne or 2-butyne.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alkynes:**

 
 
• Alkynes are hydrocarbons characterized by the presence of at least one triple bond between carbon atoms.
 
• The general formula for alkynes is CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, reflecting their unsaturation.
 
• They are more reactive than alkanes and alkenes due to the electron density of the triple bond.
 
 
 
• **Nomenclature Rules:**
 
 
• In IUPAC nomenclature, the longest continuous chain containing the triple bond is selected as the parent chain.
 
• The chain is numbered from the end nearest to the triple bond, and the position of the bond is indicated in the name.
 
 
 
• **Isomerism in Butyne:**
 
 
• **1-Butyne:** The triple bond is located between the first and second carbon atoms.
 
• **2-Butyne:** The triple bond is located between the second and third carbon atoms.
 
 
 
• **Reactivity of Alkynes:**
 
 
• Alkynes undergo addition reactions, such as hydrogenation, halogenation, and hydrohalogenation.
 
• The triple bond can also participate in oxidation and polymerization reactions.

questions.question:
A factory set up in my area is causing huge deforestation. Which of the following can we expect to see in the near future?

 A) Lowering of ground water

 B) Lower temperatures

 C) Frequent rain

 D) Arrival of new animals
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lowering of ground water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Deforestation leads to the loss of tree cover, which reduces the ability of the soil to retain water. This often results in **a lowering of the water table**.
 
• Without trees, there is **reduced groundwater recharge** as the water from rainfall flows away instead of seeping into the ground.
 
• The absence of tree roots, which help anchor the soil, can lead to **soil erosion**, further disrupting the natural water cycle.
 
• Deforestation can also lead to **decreased local humidity**, reducing the chances of rainfall and further exacerbating water scarcity.
 
• As a result, areas near deforested regions often face **water shortages** and declining groundwater levels over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deforestation:**

 
 
• Deforestation refers to the clearing or thinning of forests by humans for agriculture, urbanization, or industrial purposes.
 
• It disrupts the water cycle, biodiversity, and climate stability.
 
 
 
• **Groundwater:**
 
 
• Groundwater is the water found underground in aquifers, which supply wells and springs.
 
• It forms an essential source of water for drinking, irrigation, and industrial purposes.
 
 
 
• **Soil Erosion:**
 
 
• The removal of topsoil by water, wind, or human activity, which negatively affects soil fertility and water retention capacity.
 
• Deforestation accelerates soil erosion by removing tree roots that bind the soil together.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Deforestation on Rainfall:**
 
 
• Trees release moisture into the atmosphere through transpiration, contributing to cloud formation and rainfall.
 
• Deforestation reduces this moisture contribution, leading to lower regional rainfall levels.

questions.question: According to Article 280 of the Indian Constitution, the Finance Commission needs to be appointed for every ________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**five years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 280 of the Indian Constitution mandates the President of India to constitute a **Finance Commission every five years** or earlier if necessary.
 
• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body responsible for **recommending the distribution of financial resources** between the Union and the States.
 
• The Commission ensures **equitable sharing of taxes** and other revenues between the Centre and the States, considering the needs of each.
 
• The first Finance Commission of India was constituted in **1951**, and subsequent commissions have been constituted every five years since.
 
• The Finance Commission is composed of a chairman and **four other members** appointed by the President, with specific qualifications outlined in the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Roles of the Finance Commission**

 
 
• Recommends the allocation of taxes collected by the Union to the states.
 
• Suggests principles for determining grants-in-aid to states from the Consolidated Fund of India.
 
• Advises on measures to augment the resources of state governments to supplement the finances of local bodies.
 
 
 
• **Chairman and Members**
 
 
• The chairman of the Finance Commission is usually a person with experience in public affairs.
 
• The other four members are chosen based on expertise in economics, administration, or financial matters.
 
 
 
• **Important Finance Commissions**
 
 
• The **15th Finance Commission**, chaired by N.K. Singh, was constituted in 2017 and submitted its final report for the period 2021-26.
 
• It focused on areas such as local body funding, health sector improvements, and disaster risk management.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Financial Devolution**
 
 
• Over time, the Finance Commission’s recommendations have played a critical role in balancing regional disparities.
 
• It has ensured fiscal federalism, a key feature of India’s governance structure.

questions.question: The last Mughal emperor of India was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bahadur Shah II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bahadur Shah II**, also known as Bahadur Shah Zafar, was the last Mughal emperor of India.
 
• He reigned from **1837 to 1857**, until the British formally ended the Mughal Empire after the Revolt of 1857.
 
• Bahadur Shah Zafar was a symbolic leader of the Indian rebellion of 1857, although he had limited control over the uprising.
 
• After the suppression of the revolt, he was exiled to Rangoon (present-day Yangon, Myanmar) by the British in **1858**.
 
• Bahadur Shah Zafar was also a noted poet and is remembered for his contributions to Urdu literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revolt of 1857:**

 
 
• The Revolt of 1857, also known as India's First War of Independence, was a major uprising against British rule.
 
• It was triggered by grievances such as economic exploitation, social and religious interference, and military injustices.
 
• Bahadur Shah Zafar was proclaimed the symbolic leader of the revolt by the rebels.
 
 
 
• **End of the Mughal Empire:**
 
 
• The fall of Bahadur Shah Zafar marked the end of the Mughal Empire, which had ruled India for over three centuries.
 
• The British East India Company formally dissolved the Mughal dynasty after the revolt.
 
 
 
• **Exile to Rangoon:**
 
 
• After the suppression of the revolt, Bahadur Shah Zafar was tried by the British and exiled to Rangoon in 1858.
 
• He spent the rest of his life in exile and died in Rangoon in **1862**.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Bahadur Shah Zafar is remembered for his poetry, which expressed his pain and longing during his exile.
 
• He remains an important figure in Indian history as the last emperor and a symbol of resistance against colonial rule.

questions.question: At the __________, Neeraj Chopra became the first Indian to win a gold medal in javelin throw.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Asian Games, 2018**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Neeraj Chopra won the gold medal in the **men's javelin throw** at the **2018 Asian Games** held in Jakarta, Indonesia.
 
• He achieved this feat on **August 27, 2018**, with a record throw of **88.06 meters**.
 
• Neeraj became the first Indian to win a gold medal in javelin throw in the history of the Asian Games.
 
• This performance marked him as one of India’s most promising track and field athletes on the global stage.
 
• His gold medal at the Asian Games was a precursor to his historic gold medal at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics** in javelin throw.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asian Games:**

 
 
• The Asian Games, also known as Asiad, is a continental multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from all over Asia.
 
• The event is organized by the **Olympic Council of Asia (OCA)** and is recognized by the International Olympic Committee (IOC).
 
• The 2018 Asian Games were co-hosted by the cities of Jakarta and Palembang in Indonesia.
 
 
 
• **Neeraj Chopra's Achievements:**
 
 
• Neeraj Chopra is an Indian track and field athlete who specializes in the javelin throw.
 
• He became the **second Indian athlete to win an individual Olympic gold medal** at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.
 
• He is also the first Indian track and field athlete to win a gold medal at the World Athletics Championships (2023).
 
 
 
• **Javelin Throw:**
 
 
• Javelin throw is a track and field event where the athlete throws a spear-like implement called a javelin as far as possible.
 
• The sport requires a combination of strength, technique, and speed to achieve maximum distance.
 
• The javelin used in competitions weighs approximately 800 grams for men and 600 grams for women.
 
 
 
• **India's Performance in Athletics:**
 
 
• India has seen significant growth in athletics, with athletes like Neeraj Chopra, Hima Das, and others making their mark internationally.
 
• India's performance in track and field events has improved significantly in recent years, with a focus on better training, facilities, and coaching.

questions.question: A famous organisation Self-Employed Women's Association (SEWA) is related with which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Self-Employed Women’s Association (SEWA)** was founded in 1972 in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, by noted activist **Ela Bhatt**.
 
• SEWA is a trade union that works to empower women in the informal sector by providing them with opportunities for self-employment.
 
• It has its roots in Gujarat but has grown to include members across various states in India and even internationally.
 
• The organization focuses on promoting the welfare of poor, self-employed women such as artisans, agricultural workers, vendors, and laborers.
 
• SEWA combines the objectives of a trade union and a cooperative, focusing on full employment and self-reliance for women in unorganized sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ela Bhatt**:

 
 
• Founder of SEWA, Ela Bhatt is a renowned social activist and Gandhian.
 
• She has been awarded numerous honors, including the **Ramon Magsaysay Award** and **Padma Bhushan**.
 
• Her work focuses on women’s empowerment, poverty alleviation, and cooperative development.
 
 
 
• **Activities of SEWA**:
 
 
• SEWA provides access to microfinance, healthcare, childcare, and skill development for its members.
 
• It helps women gain access to markets and negotiate better wages.
 
• It also advocates for policy changes to support informal sector workers.
 
 
 
• **Membership and Reach**:
 
 
• As of recent data, SEWA has over 2 million members from various states in India.
 
• It has been instrumental in empowering rural and urban women in marginalized communities.
 
 
 
• **Informal Sector in India**:
 
 
• The informal sector employs a significant portion of India’s workforce, especially women.
 
• It includes jobs without formal contracts or social security, such as domestic work, street vending, and agricultural labor.
 
• Organizations like SEWA play a critical role in providing support and advocacy for workers in this sector.

questions.question: How many Pillar Edicts or Major Pillar Edicts (PEs) of Ashoka are found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ashoka, the Mauryan emperor, inscribed **seven Major Pillar Edicts** during his reign.
 
• The Pillar Edicts were inscribed on massive stone pillars across the Indian subcontinent.
 
• These edicts primarily focus on **Dhamma (moral law)** and provide guidance on ethical and moral conduct.
 
• The Major Pillar Edicts address themes such as **non-violence, religious tolerance, and welfare of people and animals**.
 
• These inscriptions are written in **Brahmi script** and were meant to be easily understood by the common people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Locations of Major Pillar Edicts:**

 
 
• The Major Pillar Edicts are found at locations such as **Topra, Meerut, Kaushambi, Rampurva, Lauriya-Nandangarh, and Sanchi**.
 
 
 
• **Ashokan Inscriptions:**
 
 
• Ashoka's inscriptions are classified into **Major Rock Edicts, Minor Rock Edicts, Major Pillar Edicts, and Minor Pillar Edicts**.
 
 
 
• **Brahmi Script:**
 
 
• The Brahmi script, used in the edicts, is one of the earliest known scripts in India and was deciphered by **James Prinsep in 1837**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Edicts:**
 
 
• The edicts reflect Ashoka's commitment to **spreading Buddhist values** and his efforts to promote **peace and harmony** across his empire.
 
 
 
• **Material and Construction:**
 
 
• The pillars are made of **polished sandstone** and are considered architectural marvels of the Mauryan period.

questions.question: In which year was the first Socio Economic and Caste Census (SECC) conducted in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2011**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first Socio Economic and Caste Census (SECC) in India was conducted in **2011** after the regular decennial Census.
 
• The SECC 2011 was a joint effort by the Ministry of Rural Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, and the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.
 
• The SECC was aimed at collecting detailed data on **various socio-economic parameters** and caste information of households across rural and urban India.
 
• This was the first time such a census was conducted since the decennial Census of 1931, which included caste-based data.
 
• The SECC 2011 data was used for formulating policies, targeting welfare schemes, and understanding the socio-economic diversity of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Purpose of SECC:**

 
 
• The SECC aimed to identify households living below the poverty line (BPL) for targeted government schemes.
 
• It collected data on income, housing, education, employment, and other socio-economic indicators.
 
 
 
• **Census vs. SECC:**
 
 
• The Census collects general population data every 10 years, whereas SECC collects detailed socio-economic and caste-specific data.
 
• The SECC focuses on identifying socio-economic disparities, while the Census provides a demographic snapshot of the country.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in SECC:**
 
 
• The SECC faced issues like data inaccuracies, underreporting, and political sensitivities over caste data.
 
• There were debates about the publication and usage of caste-related data.
 
 
 
• **SECC 2011 Data Usage:**
 
 
• The SECC 2011 data was used for schemes like Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, MGNREGA, and others.
 
• Data helped in better targeting of benefits to the most deserving sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Future of SECC:**
 
 
• There have been discussions on conducting updated SECCs to address socio-economic changes and policy needs.
 
• However, concerns about privacy and data accuracy remain key challenges.

questions.question: In May 2023, who was sworn in as Central Vigilance Commissioner?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Praveen Kumar Srivastava**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Praveen Kumar Srivastava was sworn in as the **Central Vigilance Commissioner (CVC) of India** in May 2023.
 
• He succeeded **Suresh N. Patel**, who completed his tenure as the CVC.
 
• Praveen Kumar Srivastava is a retired **Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer** from the Assam-Meghalaya cadre of the 1988 batch.
 
• Before his appointment, he served as the **Vigilance Commissioner in the Central Vigilance Commission** from February 2023.
 
• The Central Vigilance Commission is the apex body for monitoring **anti-corruption measures and ensuring integrity in public administration.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Vigilance Commission (CVC):**

 
 
• Established in 1964 through an executive resolution based on the recommendations of the **Santhanam Committee on Corruption Prevention.**
 
• It is a statutory body under the **Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.**
 
• The CVC is responsible for supervising the vigilance administration and advising the central government on vigilance matters.
 
• The commission consists of a **Central Vigilance Commissioner and two Vigilance Commissioners.**
 
 
 
• **Functions of the CVC:**
 
 
• Monitoring and investigating cases of corruption involving public servants and government officials.
 
• Overseeing the functioning of the **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)** in cases related to corruption.
 
• Advising central government departments on vigilance and anti-corruption measures.
 
 
 
• **Vigilance Awareness Week:**
 
 
• Observed every year to promote integrity and transparency in public administration.
 
• It is organized by the CVC during the birth anniversary week of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (October 31).
 
 
 
• **Appointment Process of CVC:**
 
 
• The Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners are appointed by the President of India.
 
• The selection is based on the recommendation of a committee comprising the **Prime Minister, Home Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.**

questions.question: Who among the following is the author of the book, 'A History of British India'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**James Mill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **James Mill**, a Scottish historian, economist, and philosopher, is the author of the book *'A History of British India.'*
 
• The book was first published in **1817** and is considered a landmark in colonial historiography.
 
• It provides a detailed account of the history, culture, and governance of India, primarily from a British perspective.
 
• James Mill divided Indian history into three periods: Hindu, Muslim, and British, a framework that has been widely debated and criticized by modern historians.
 
• This work significantly influenced the British colonial administration's policies and their perception of India during the 19th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **James Mill (1773–1836):**

 
 
• A Scottish historian, economist, and political theorist known for his utilitarian philosophy.
 
• He was the father of John Stuart Mill, a prominent philosopher and advocate of liberty.
 
 
 
• **Colonial Historiography:**
 
 
• Refers to the historical writing and analysis of colonial rule, often from the colonizer's perspective.
 
• James Mill's work is an example of this, portraying India as stagnant and in need of reform under British rule.
 
 
 
• **Criticism of Mill's Work:**
 
 
• Modern historians criticize Mill’s framework for oversimplifying Indian history and ignoring its diversity.
 
• His portrayal of Indian society as backward and despotic justified British colonial intervention.
 
 
 
• **Impact on British Policy:**
 
 
• Mill's book heavily influenced British administrators, including those in the East India Company, shaping their governance of India.
 
• It reinforced the perception of India as a society needing British-led "civilization."

questions.question: Bharatanatyam dancer ________ received the Natya Kala Sarathy award from Sri Parthasarathy Swami Sabha in 2023 at Chennai.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Srekala Bharath**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Srekala Bharath, a renowned Bharatanatyam dancer, was honored with the **Natya Kala Sarathy award** in 2023.
 
• The award was presented by the **Sri Parthasarathy Swami Sabha**, one of the oldest and most prestigious cultural organizations in Chennai.
 
• Srekala Bharath is known for her contributions to the preservation and promotion of the **Bharatanatyam dance form**.
 
• The Natya Kala Sarathy award recognizes individuals for their exemplary achievements in the field of classical dance.
 
• The award ceremony was held in Chennai, a hub for classical arts and culture in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**

 
 
• An Indian classical dance form originating from Tamil Nadu, Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest dance traditions in the world.
 
• It is characterized by intricate footwork, graceful movements, and expressions (abhinaya) that narrate stories from Hindu mythology.
 
• Bharatanatyam is often performed in temples as a form of devotion and is deeply rooted in spiritual themes.
 
 
 
• **Sri Parthasarathy Swami Sabha**
 
 
• Founded in 1900, it is one of the oldest cultural institutions in India.
 
• The Sabha is committed to promoting and preserving Indian classical music, dance, and drama.
 
• It organizes annual events and festivals to honor artists and provide a platform for cultural expression.
 
 
 
• **Natya Kala Sarathy Award**
 
 
• This award is presented by Sri Parthasarathy Swami Sabha to recognize outstanding contributions to classical dance.
 
• It celebrates the dedication and artistry of individuals who have enriched the performing arts.
 
• Winners are selected based on their body of work, influence on the art form, and commitment to cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Chennai: A Cultural Hub**
 
 
• Chennai, also known as the cultural capital of South India, is renowned for its patronage of classical arts.
 
• The city hosts prestigious events like the Margazhi Festival, drawing performers and audiences from around the globe.
 
• It is home to numerous art institutions and sabhas that play a pivotal role in preserving India's rich cultural legacy.
